_why:
COUNT CORRECTED 73 -> 78 -> 79 on 2026-09-19. `text_overlays` was a FAMILY in the live pipeline and was missing from this file entirely. Its real variant list came from the schema's OWN HISTORY (handler.py @42df870: torn_paper, sticky_note, quote_card, lower_third, caption_match), not from the current enum — which had been pruned to two while _TextOverlay kept carrying topText/bottomText, quote/attribution and text, the fields of the three retired ones. A family reads as two variants and is five. The filename keeps its historical number; this key is the count. COUNT 78 -> 79 on 2026-09-19: PlainText added as the SIXTH variant. It is not in the old schema's list, and it is not a new idea either — it is the shape Builder-2 measured as the references' most common text (plain, medium, middle). CaptionMatch served that shape for one day only because its port was incomplete: it rendered a fixed sans-serif and never read the caption style it is named for. Once CaptionMatch honoured the edit's chosen style, the plain shape left the menu with it, so the workhorse gets its own component named for what it is.

COUNT CORRECTED 79 -> 77 on 2026-09-20, and the two are a phantom and an omission in the SAME family.

THREE ENTRIES NAMED COMPONENTS THAT DO NOT EXIST. DeviceMockup, EmojiCard and EvidenceCard were listed under motion graphic with NO body in ported_mg/ and NO entry in chatcut_registry.json -- not even in its "refused" list, which is where a component that was built and rejected goes. They are not refused, they are ABSENT. They appear in Builder-1's 51a2b2f as the families that "were waiting for" the source-layer capability, and somewhere between being unblocked and being built they were written down as though the unblocking had built them. A capability that MAKES a component possible is not the component.

AND ONE THAT DOES EXIST WAS MISSING. SpeechBubble has a body in ported_mg/ and sits in the registry's refused list, and was in no family here at all. So the same family was over-counted by three and under-counted by one, which nets to two -- and that is exactly why a NET figure is the wrong thing to check: had either error been one larger they would have cancelled, the total would have stayed 79, and the file would have read correct while naming three things that do not exist.

THE LIST IS NOW DERIVED FROM ported_mg/ RATHER THAN MAINTAINED BESIDE IT. A hand-kept list of the things that exist drifts from the things that exist; that is the whole defect. 29 bodies, 29 names.

EVERY OTHER FAMILY WAS CHECKED AGAINST ITS OWN ARTIFACTS, so this is a count and not a re-assertion:
  zoom 7               7 of 7 have a body in port/bodies/
  transition 9         9 of 9 have a body
  tight-cut overlay 2  2 of 2 have a body (ShutterFlashOverlay, LightLeakOverlay)
  text overlay 6       6 of 6 have a body
  sfx 15               15 of 15 staged as ChatCut assets with a measured attack
  caption style 9      9 of 9 have a file in ported_captions/
  motion graphic 29    29 of 29, derived above
NAMES CORRECTED 2026-09-21, and the count did not move.

The `tight-cut overlay` family listed `LightLeak` and `ShutterFlash`. The
components are `LightLeakOverlay` and `ShutterFlashOverlay` — that is what the
bodies in port/bodies/ are called, what transition_properties.json keys, and
what is registered in ChatCut. This file's OWN derivation note two paragraphs up
already named them correctly; the list and the note disagreed and nobody read
them together.

IT WAS NOT A COSMETIC DIFFERENCE. `ShutterFlash` is ALSO a transition, and it is
a DIFFERENT COMPONENT with a different body. So one name sat in two families,
and the first thing to look components up BY NAME — the inventory's picture
field — gave the overlay the TRANSITION's still and reported 14 of 15 pictured
while showing ShutterFlash twice. A wrong picture is worse than a missing one:
the missing one is counted.

Same shape as the three phantom motion graphics, one level along: that was a
name with no component, this is one component's name worn by two.
STICKYNOTES IS ONE COMPONENT WITH TWO HOMES, and the arc that established it is
recorded in collision_quarantine.json rather than here. Short version: the
collision check found the name in two families, I reported it as two components,
it was renamed apart, and the rename was REVERSED because handler.py:8287 had
always said "ONE COMPONENT, TWO HOMES - route it, never duplicate it" and was
right. It is declared in `_two_home` above, and the collision check reads that
declaration instead of counting the name as a duplicate.

SO THERE ARE TWO COUNTS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER. A component in two
families occupies two family placements and is still one component. Both are
stated, because naming only one is how a number starts meaning whichever the
reader assumed.
THE THREE PHANTOMS ARE REAL NOW, 2026-09-21, and that closes the 79 -> 77
correction from the other end. DeviceMockup, EmojiCard and EvidenceCard were
listed as motion graphics with NO body and no registry entry — not even a
refusal — so I removed them. They have bodies today: port/bodies/*.jsx, a
property table in port/frame_composition_properties.json, registered in ChatCut
and drawn on a corpus still. They go back as their OWN family rather than under
motion graphic, because what they have in common is the thing that was never
true of the phantoms: each one TAKES A STILL and composes a frame around it.

Removing them was right and adding them back is not a reversal of it. A name
with no component is a phantom whatever the component would have been; the entry
had to go before the thing could exist.
COMPONENTS 79.
TOTAL 80.
